CFML Language Reference: Functions

CreateDate

Builds a date/time value from three numbers. The time part is midnight (00:00:00).

Category

Date and time functions

Syntax

CreateDate(year, month, day)

Parameters

year
Four-digit year, from 100 to 9999.
month
Month, 1 to 12.
day
Day of the month, 1 to the last day of that month.

Returns

A date/time value. Printed directly it looks like {ts '1999-10-22 00:00:00'}.

Usage

Every part is checked: February 29, 1999 or month 13 throws an "Invalid date." error that you can catch with CFTRY/CFCATCH. Two-digit years use the same sliding window as date strings: 0 to 29 become 2000 to 2029 and 30 to 99 become 1930 to 1999, so CreateDate(99, 12, 31) is New Year's Eve 1999, not A.D. 99. Write four digits anyway; it is the year 2000 problem in miniature.

When you output a date/time value without formatting, you get the ODBC timestamp form {ts '...'}. Wrap it in DateFormat or TimeFormat for anything a human will read. To add a time, use CreateDateTime.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Launch = CreateDate(1999, 10, 22)>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Expression</TH><TH>Result</TH></TR>
<TR><TD>CreateDate(1999, 10, 22)</TD><TD>#Launch#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>DateFormat(...)</TD><TD>#DateFormat(Launch, "dddd, mmmm d, yyyy")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Year / Month / Day</TD><TD>#Year(Launch)# / #Month(Launch)# / #Day(Launch)#</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
</CFOUTPUT>

<!--- Invalid dates throw an error --->
<CFTRY>
  <CFSET Bad = CreateDate(1999, 2, 29)>
<CFCATCH TYPE="Expression">
  <CFOUTPUT><P>CreateDate(1999, 2, 29): <B>#CFCATCH.Message#</B> 1999 was not a leap year.</P></CFOUTPUT>
</CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>

See also

CreateDateTime, CreateTime, CreateODBCDate, DateFormat, ParseDateTime
